rows.title: Obstructive Sleep Apnea in Acromegaly and the Effect of Treatment: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
rows.evidenceMatch: Directly evaluates obstructive sleep apnea in acromegaly, including OSA prevalence/AHI and longitudinal pre/post-treatment AHI. The implemented guard already limits the broad sleep-apnea taxonomy target to OSA, requires separately established OSA, and prohibits automatic individual causation.
rows.limitations: Active versus inactive acromegaly did not show a significant cross-sectional difference in OSA prevalence or AHI; the strongest longitudinal finding is improvement in AHI after acromegaly treatment. Therefore the source supports a bounded comorbidity/association and treatment-response proposition, not automatic individual causation.

rows.title: Prevalence of extra-articular manifestations in patients with ankylosing spondylitis: a systematic review and meta-analysis
rows.evidenceMatch: Directly supports uveitis as a common extra-articular manifestation in ankylosing spondylitis and reports a pooled uveitis prevalence of 25.8%. The implemented guard requires ophthalmic diagnosis and preserves alternative causes.
rows.limitations: This is prevalence/association evidence with substantial heterogeneity across studies; it does not establish individual causation.

rows.title: Bone metabolism in primary hyperparathyroidism
rows.evidenceMatch: Directly addresses primary hyperparathyroidism skeletal disease: increased bone remodeling/resorption, declining BMD, compromised bone quality, increased fracture risk, and reported osteoporosis in PHPT cohorts. The implemented guard restricts the relationship to primary hyperparathyroidism and requires separately established osteoporosis.
rows.limitations: The article is a review rather than a dedicated systematic review of osteoporosis incidence. Existing phenotype and diagnostic guards are therefore important and sufficient; no further narrowing is required.

rows.title: Bone Mineral Density Improvement After Resolution of Endogenous Cushing Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
rows.evidenceMatch: Directly restricted to endogenous Cushing syndrome and demonstrates significant lumbar-spine and femoral-neck BMD improvement after resolution. The paper frames the findings as relevant to endogenous-Cushing-associated osteoporosis. This precisely matches the implemented endogenous-Cushing restriction.
rows.limitations: The meta-analysis evaluates BMD change after disease resolution; sample size was 302 across 12 studies and lumbar-spine estimates showed substantial heterogeneity. The implemented guard already requires separately established osteoporosis and excludes exogenous glucocorticoid-only disease.

rows.title: Epidemiology, prognosis, and challenges in the management of hyperthyroidism-related atrial fibrillation
rows.evidenceMatch: Directly states that atrial fibrillation is the most common cardiac complication of hyperthyroidism, occurring in 5-15% of overtly hyperthyroid patients, and describes frequent spontaneous reversion after restoration of euthyroidism. The implemented guard limits the broad cardiac-arrhythmia target to documented atrial fibrillation.
rows.limitations: The source is AF-specific and does not support generalization to all arrhythmias. The existing AF-only guard fully addresses that limitation.
